escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: Nortech wants two rules applied in every conversation in a client repo: "use TypeScript strict mode" and "never commit directly to main." Where should these rules live?
opciones: A skill whose description mentions "coding rules and git workflow"
A SessionStart hook that prints the rules
The repository's CLAUDE.md file
A custom subagent with the rules in its system prompt
preguntas.explicacion: C. Reglas que aplican siempre, en toda conversación → CLAUDE.md (always-on). Una skill cargaría solo si hay matching (A); el hook de B imprime pero no gobierna el razonamiento continuo; el subagent (D) solo aplica al delegar.

escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: The team's release-notes procedure is a detailed 12-step process used about once per sprint. Developers complain that keeping it always loaded clutters the context. What should Nortech do?
opciones: Keep it in CLAUDE.md but shorten it
Move it to a project skill in .claude/skills so it loads on demand
Convert it to a PostToolUse hook
Expose it as an MCP server tool
preguntas.explicacion: B. "Detailed procedures that would clutter every conversation" es una de las 3 razones literales para usar skills: carga on-demand cuando pides release notes. Acortarlo (A) pierde detalle; no es un evento (C) ni una herramienta externa (D).

escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: Nortech's security team requires that a secret scanner runs before every git commit Claude executes — it may never be skipped, regardless of what the user asked. What guarantees this?
opciones: A PreToolUse hook matching the commit tool call
A skill described as "scans for secrets before commits"
A CLAUDE.md rule: "always scan for secrets before committing"
Training developers to request the scan manually
preguntas.explicacion: A. "Never be skipped" = necesitas garantía determinista → hook (event-driven, puede incluso bloquear con exit code 2). Skills y CLAUDE.md dependen del criterio de Claude — probabilístico. Tu regla: ¿frase o suceso? Esto es un suceso.

escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: A developer keeps a personal code-review skill in ~/.claude/skills. The client repo also ships a project code-review skill. When the developer asks for a review in that repo, what happens?
opciones: The project skill applies — project settings are more specific
Both skills merge into one instruction set
Claude Code reports a conflict and asks the developer to choose
The personal skill applies — Personal outranks Project in the priority order
preguntas.explicacion: D. Prioridad E-P-P-P: Enterprise → Personal → Project → Plugins. La trampa es A ("más específico"): la intuición falla, Personal gana a Project. No hay merge ni diálogo.

escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: Nortech wants every developer to receive the release-notes skill automatically, with updates arriving through their normal workflow. What's the simplest method?
opciones: Email the skill folder and have each developer copy it to ~/.claude/skills
Commit the skill to .claude/skills in the repository — cloning and pulling distribute it
Publish it to a public marketplace as a plugin
Deploy it through enterprise managed settings
preguntas.explicacion: B. El método "simplest" de la lección 5: commit al repo — quien clona la recibe, `git pull` trae updates. Plugin (C) es para alcance multi-repo/comunidad; enterprise (D) para obligatoriedad organizacional.

escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: A year later, Nortech's compliance department decides the security-review skill MUST be identical across the whole organization and no developer may override it with a same-named skill. What now?
opciones: Publish it as a plugin on an internal marketplace
Commit it to every repository's .claude/skills
Deploy it organization-wide via enterprise managed settings
Ask developers to delete their personal copies
preguntas.explicacion: C. Keyword "MUST" + "no override" → enterprise managed settings: prioridad máxima, pisa personal/project/plugin del mismo nombre. Repo y plugin quedan por debajo de Personal en prioridad — un dev podría taparlas.

escenario.texto: Nortech Solutions is a 12-developer consultancy standardizing how its teams use Claude Code across client projects. They are deciding where each piece of team knowledge and automation should live, and how to distribute it.

preguntas.stem: Nortech builds a custom subagent, release-auditor, in .claude/agents and expects it to use the team's release-notes skill. The subagent never applies it. What's the most likely fix?
opciones: List the skill explicitly in the agent's skills: frontmatter field — subagents don't inherit skills
Upgrade the agent's model field to a larger model
Add allowed-tools to the skill so subagents can access it
Nothing — subagents can never use skills
preguntas.explicacion: A. El gotcha de la lección 5: los subagents nacen con contexto limpio y no heredan skills — hay que listarlas en `skills:`. D es la trampa: los built-in no pueden nunca, pero los custom sí, listándolas.

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: An engineer created ~/.claude/skills/SKILL.md with valid frontmatter, but the skill never appears in the available skills list. Why?
opciones: The file must be renamed to skill.md (lowercase)
SKILL.md must live inside a named directory (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/sql-optimizer/SKILL.md), not at the skills root
Skills without allowed-tools are not loaded
Personal skills require a plugin wrapper to load
preguntas.explicacion: B. Requisito estructural de la lección 6: SKILL.md dentro de un directorio con nombre, nunca suelto en la raíz de skills/. El nombre correcto es justamente SKILL.md en mayúsculas (A al revés). Diagnóstico: `claude --debug`.

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: The sql-optimizer skill passes the validator and appears in the list, but asking "why is this query slow?" never triggers it. Its description reads: "Optimizes SQL." What's the fix?
opciones: Rename the skill — a higher-priority skill is shadowing it
Give the skill's scripts execute permission
Shorten the SKILL.md below 500 lines
Expand the description with real trigger phrases ("why is this slow?", "make this query faster") and test variations
preguntas.explicacion: D. "No se dispara" → la causa es "almost always the description": el matching semántico necesita overlap con cómo pides las cosas. "Optimizes SQL" no se parece a "why is this query slow?".

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: Claude keeps activating db-review when engineers want sql-optimizer, and vice versa. What does the course recommend?
opciones: Make the two descriptions more distinct and specific
Delete one of the two skills
Move one skill to enterprise level so priority decides
Merge both into a single skill
preguntas.explicacion: A. "Wrong skill gets used" → descriptions demasiado parecidas; hacerlas distintas. La especificidad ayuda al matching Y evita conflictos con skills de nombre/tema similar.

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: Per the course, what should the team try FIRST when a skill misbehaves, before spending time on any other debugging?
opciones: Run claude --debug and read the startup log
Reinstall Claude Code
Run the skills validator (installable with uv) to catch structural problems
Clear the plugin cache
preguntas.explicacion: C. "The first thing to try is the agent skills verifier command" — el validator atrapa problemas estructurales antes de perder tiempo. `claude --debug` (A) es el segundo paso, para errores de carga.

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: A skill loads but its bundled script fails at runtime on Windows. The SKILL.md references scripts\check.py and the file was copied without execute permission. Which pair of fixes does the course prescribe?
opciones: Rename SKILL.md to skill.md and restart Claude Code
Use forward slashes (scripts/check.py) everywhere — even on Windows — and chmod +x the script
Paste the script's code into SKILL.md so no file is needed
Move the script to assets/ and reference it from the description
preguntas.explicacion: B. Runtime errors: dependencias instaladas (y anotadas en la description) · chmod +x a los scripts · forward slashes ( / ) en todas las rutas, incluso en Windows. C destruiría la ventaja de contexto de los scripts.

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: DataFlow needs an audit skill that can inspect code but must be structurally prevented from modifying any file while active. How?
opciones: Write "do not edit files" prominently in the skill's instructions
Set model: haiku so the skill is less capable
Omit allowed-tools so Claude asks permission for everything
Set allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob in the frontmatter
preguntas.explicacion: D. `allowed-tools` con lista de solo-lectura = guardrail estructural: sin editar, sin escribir. Una instrucción en prosa (A) es un consejo, no una barrera. Omitirlo (C) NO restringe nada — usa el modelo de permisos normal.

escenario.texto: DataFlow Inc. is rolling out a set of database-related skills to its analytics team. The rollout hits several problems that the team must diagnose and fix.

preguntas.stem: Another skill's frontmatter has only name and description. What can Claude do with tools while that skill is active?
opciones: Whatever its normal permission model allows — omitting allowed-tools imposes no restriction
Nothing — a skill without allowed-tools cannot use tools
Read-only tools by default
Only tools named inside the skill's instructions
preguntas.explicacion: A. Trampa clásica: omitir `allowed-tools` = sin restricción (modelo de permisos normal), no "sin herramientas". Solo restringe cuando el campo existe.

escenario.texto: Vertex Analytics is designing its Claude Code architecture from scratch: deciding which mechanism handles each need, and keeping the context window efficient as the setup grows.

preguntas.stem: Vertex wants Claude to run live queries against its production Postgres database during conversations. Which mechanism provides this?
opciones: A skill containing the database schema and SQL best practices
An MCP server connected to the database
A PostToolUse hook that runs queries after each edit
Pasting the schema into CLAUDE.md
preguntas.explicacion: B. Lo que falta son manos, no conocimiento: acceso a un sistema externo → MCP ("a different category entirely"). Una skill (A) le enseñaría SQL, pero no le da por dónde entrar a la base.

escenario.texto: Vertex Analytics is designing its Claude Code architecture from scratch: deciding which mechanism handles each need, and keeping the context window efficient as the setup grows.

preguntas.stem: Vertex's main skill has grown to 2,200 lines; most of it is edge-case reference tables that rarely apply. Following the open standard, what should they do?
opciones: Split it into two differently-named skills
Set a larger model in the frontmatter to handle the length
Keep SKILL.md under ~500 lines and move the tables to references/ files linked with an explicit "Only load when..." condition
Rewrite the tables as shorter prose to reduce the line count
preguntas.explicacion: C. Progressive disclosure: SKILL.md como índice (<500 líneas) y el detalle en `references/` con condición explícita de carga. No se recorta contenido (D) — se decide cuándo entra. "A table of contents in the context window."

escenario.texto: Vertex Analytics is designing its Claude Code architecture from scratch: deciding which mechanism handles each need, and keeping the context window efficient as the setup grows.

preguntas.stem: A monthly data normalization must produce byte-identical output every run, and the team wants it cheap in context. Best approach inside the skill?
opciones: A tested script in scripts/, with SKILL.md instructing "run the script, not read it" — only its output consumes tokens
Detailed instructions in SKILL.md so Claude writes the transformation code fresh each run
A references/ file describing the algorithm for Claude to follow
A subagent with a top-tier model to minimize mistakes
preguntas.explicacion: A. Dos razones de los scripts: determinismo (código probado = mismo resultado siempre; código generado varía) y contexto (solo el output consume — 300 líneas de código pueden costar 3 de salida).

escenario.texto: Vertex Analytics is designing its Claude Code architecture from scratch: deciding which mechanism handles each need, and keeping the context window efficient as the setup grows.

preguntas.stem: Vertex needs to scan ~300 files for uses of a deprecated API and get a summary — without flooding the main conversation's context. Which mechanism?
opciones: A skill with instructions for searching the codebase
A PreToolUse hook that greps on every tool call
A CLAUDE.md section listing the deprecated APIs
Delegate to a subagent — it works in an isolated context and returns only the results
preguntas.explicacion: D. Lo que falta es espacio: tarea grande y cerrada → subagent. Los 300 archivos viven en SU contexto; a ti solo te llega el resumen. Una skill (A) sumaría conocimiento pero el trabajo seguiría inflando TU contexto.

escenario.texto: Vertex Analytics is designing its Claude Code architecture from scratch: deciding which mechanism handles each need, and keeping the context window efficient as the setup grows.

preguntas.stem: When a custom subagent declares skills: data-quality, sql-style in its frontmatter, when do those skills load?
opciones: On demand, when the subagent's task matches each description
All of them at subagent start — which is why only always-relevant skills should be listed
Only after the user confirms each skill
They never load — subagents cannot use skills
preguntas.explicacion: B. En subagents las skills cargan al arrancar, todas completas — no hay matching on-demand ni confirmación ahí. Por eso la regla: "only list skills that are always relevant to the subagent's purpose".

preguntas.stem: A Vertex engineer tries to make the built-in Explore agent use the team's review skill. What's the reality?
opciones: It works if the skill is listed in settings.json
It works if the skill is deployed at enterprise level
Impossible — built-in agents can't access skills at all; only custom subagents in .claude/agents can, by listing them
It works automatically since Explore inherits the main context
preguntas.explicacion: C. Distinción de la lección 5: built-in agents (Explore, Plan, Verify) no pueden usar skills en absoluto; solo los custom subagents, y solo listándolas explícitamente.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: Three hours into a session the context window is nearly full. The debugging phase ended long ago; only the payment-API migration matters now. What's the best move?
opciones: Run /compact with nothing else — the summary handles itself
Run /compact Focus on the payment-API migration so the summary keeps what matters
Start a brand-new session and re-explain everything
Rewind to the first checkpoint of the session
preguntas.explicacion: B. Lo que escribes después de /compact moldea el resumen — *"your steering wheel for context"*. A secas (A) arriesga que el resumen tire lo importante y Claude derive. Regla práctica: di qué CONSERVAR.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: Claude took a wrong approach three prompts ago and edited several files since. You want both the files AND the conversation back to that point. What do you do?
opciones: Run /compact targeting that earlier point
Run git reset yourself and keep chatting
Choose "Summarize from here" in the rewind menu
Double-tap Escape on an empty prompt and choose "Restore code and conversation"
preguntas.explicacion: D. Cada prompt tuyo crea un checkpoint; doble Escape abre el menú rewind, y "Restore code and conversation" regresa AMBOS. /compact nunca toca archivos; git reset (B) deja el chat contaminado con el enfoque malo.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: The team wants Claude to keep working until the job is truly finished. Given that the /goal evaluator only reads the transcript, which condition will actually work?
opciones: /goal the UI feels snappier
/goal the code quality is clearly better
/goal pytest reports 0 failures and mypy reports 0 errors
/goal our users are happier with the app
preguntas.explicacion: C. El evaluador solo lee la transcripción: la condición debe ser verificable en el output que Claude imprime (resultados de tests, type checker). "Se siente mejor" no aparece en ningún output.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: Two parallel Claude sessions on the same repo keep overwriting each other's files, and when the team tried separate copies, the new tree lacked the git-ignored .env file and nothing ran. What's the correct setup?
opciones: Run each session in its own worktree, and list .env in a .worktreeinclude file at the repo root
Keep both sessions in the same folder but switch them to accept-edits mode
Commit the .env file so every copy has it
Alternate sessions manually so only one runs at a time
preguntas.explicacion: A. Worktrees = árboles independientes ("despensa común, cocinas separadas"), y .worktreeinclude existe exactamente para copiar archivos git-ignored (.env, config local) a cada árbol nuevo. Commitear secretos (C) viola toda práctica — y el CLAUDE.md de tu propia maqueta.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: A developer has a User CLAUDE.md, the repo has Project and Local files, and the org deploys a managed policy file. At launch, what does Claude Code load?
opciones: Only the highest-priority file — managed policy wins and the rest are dropped
Project overrides User; Local overrides Project
All four load together and stack — nothing gets dropped
The user picks one at session start
preguntas.explicacion: C. El contraste clave con skills: los CLAUDE.md no compiten — se apilan ("they stack, nothing gets dropped"). La prioridad E-P-P-P es de skills con nombre repetido, no de CLAUDE.md.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: A teammate split a 1,200-line CLAUDE.md into six files loaded with @.claude/conventions/... imports and claims the context load dropped dramatically. What's the reality?
opciones: Correct — imported files load only when a task needs them
False — imports expand inline at launch; they organize the content but everything still loads up front
Correct — imports load only name and description like skills do
False — imports are ignored entirely by Claude Code
preguntas.explicacion: B. 🪤 La trampa perfecta: suena a progressive disclosure pero es lo contrario. *"Use imports to organize, not to shrink the load."* La carga diferida real es de las skills, no de los imports de CLAUDE.md.

escenario.texto: Helix Labs runs multi-hour Claude Code refactoring sessions on a large monorepo. The team is learning to steer long runs and to configure Claude so sessions stay on course without babysitting.

preguntas.stem: Helix's verification skill runs the test suite after each refactor and everything is green — yet a bug shipped because a test had been quietly loosened to always pass. Per the course, what step was missing?
opciones: Reading the diff to check that no test was weakened just to make things pass
Running the tests twice to confirm the results
Using a bigger model for the verification skill
Asking Claude to summarize what it changed
preguntas.explicacion: A. La cadena completa: correr tests → leer el diff → verificar que ningún test fue debilitado → reportar con evidencia. Verde no basta: *"Done is the gates being run and observed."*

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: An overnight pipeline runs Claude Code with no human available. Any action outside the pre-approved tool list should be denied immediately so the pipeline never hangs waiting for approval. Which permission mode?
opciones: Manual
Accept edits
Bypass permissions
Don't ask
preguntas.explicacion: D. "Don't ask": solo tools pre-aprobadas; lo demás se auto-deniega sin prompt — el pipeline sigue avanzando. Ese es el punto: sin humano, un prompt de aprobación = pipeline colgado.

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: An auto-mode run finished with every action approved by the classifier, yet the refactored authentication code is broken. Why didn't the classifier stop it, and what closes the gap?
opciones: The classifier was misconfigured; reinstall Claude Code
The classifier guards intent, not correctness — pair auto mode with a Stop hook that runs the tests
Auto mode disables all safety review; use bypass instead
The classifier only reviews bash commands, not code edits
preguntas.explicacion: B. *"Broken isn't dangerous."* El clasificador vigila escaladas de intención ANTES de cada acción; la corrección la garantiza el Stop hook DESPUÉS. Uno intención, otro corrección — el par de las lecciones 4+5.

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: When is "bypass permissions" an acceptable choice, per the course?
opciones: Only inside an isolated container or virtual machine
Whenever you fully trust the prompt you wrote
On any CI runner, since CI is already automated
Never — the flag exists only for Anthropic internal testing
preguntas.explicacion: A. Bypass = cero checks (equivalente a dangerously-skip-permissions). Solo en un entorno aislado y desechable: contenedor o VM.

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: A PreToolUse hook detects a dangerous command and exits with code 1 to stop it. What actually happens?
opciones: The command is blocked and stderr goes to Claude
Claude Code crashes with a hook error
Nothing is blocked — the command runs anyway; blocking requires exit code 2
The user gets an approval prompt
preguntas.explicacion: C. 🪤 LA trampa de exit codes: 1 no bloquea (se loguea y Claude sigue). Bloquear = exit 2, cuyo stderr sí se alimenta a Claude como contexto.

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: After long conversations get compacted, Claude "starts cold" and forgets which files were in play. Which hook setup re-injects a working-state summary into the conversation?
opciones: A PostCompact hook that prints the summary
A PreCompact hook that saves the summary to a file
A Stop hook with exit code 2
A SessionStart hook with the compact matcher — its output goes back into context
preguntas.explicacion: D. El trip-up oficial del curso: PostCompact NO devuelve su output a la conversación; SessionStart con matcher compact sí. (Texto plano en exit 0 entra al contexto en SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/UserPromptExpansion.)

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: A command Claude wants to run contains a live secret (sk_live_...). The work itself is legitimate. What's the most elegant PreToolUse response?
opciones: permissionDecision "deny" — refuse the whole command
Return updatedInput with the secret replaced by a placeholder — the command still runs, the secret never gets through (echoing back the unchanged fields)
permissionDecision "ask" so the user approves the secret
Exit code 1 with a warning in stderr
preguntas.explicacion: B. Redactar en vez de bloquear: updatedInput reescribe la llamada. Catch: reemplaza el input COMPLETO — devuelve también los campos que no cambias. *"The work still got done. But the secret never made it through."*

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: Meridian wants a routine that runs every 15 minutes and pushes straight to main. What's wrong with this plan?
opciones: Recurring routines run at most hourly, and runs can only push to claude/ prefixed branches unless loosened per repo
Nothing — routines support any interval and any branch
Routines can't be scheduled; they only respond to GitHub events
Routines require you to host your own server for cron triggers
preguntas.explicacion: A. Dos de los 3 límites de routines: recurrencia máximo cada hora, y clone fresco que solo pushea a ramas claude/ — el guardrail anti-"reescribir main". (El tercero: es research preview.) Y no: corren en infra de Anthropic, sin servidor tuyo.

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: A CI script needs the fastest possible startup and must NOT load the repo's hooks, skills, MCP servers, or CLAUDE.md. Per the official docs, which invocation is correct?
opciones: claude -p "..." — the -p flag skips all auto-discovery
claude --headless "..."
claude --bare -p "..." — --bare is what skips auto-discovery
claude --no-context -p "..."
preguntas.explicacion: C. Verificado contra docs oficiales: --bare se salta la auto-discovery (hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, auto memory, CLAUDE.md); -p a secas SÍ carga el entorno local. (La página del curso tiene este dato mal; el video bien.)

escenario.texto: Meridian Ops is moving its repetitive work to unattended automation: overnight jobs, CI pipelines, and scheduled audits, with guardrails that hold when nobody is watching.

preguntas.stem: A pipeline needs Claude to emit a machine-readable list of endpoints matching a schema, to pipe into a database. Which setup, and where does the data land?
opciones: Ask for JSON in the prompt and parse whatever comes back
--output-format json --json-schema '...' — the schema-matching object lands in the structured_output field
--format=xml with a stylesheet
Redirect stdout to a .json file; Claude auto-detects the extension
preguntas.explicacion: B. El schema RESTRINGE la salida (no es una súplica en el prompt) y el objeto cae en structured_output → jq '.structured_output.endpoints' → a la base de datos.

escenario.texto: Atlas Team is rolling Claude into its GitHub workflow — managed code review, a custom action, and shared plugins — while keeping unsupervised results trustworthy.

preguntas.stem: Atlas wants managed Code Review to auto-fix findings and block any PR with critical issues from merging. What's the reality of the managed service?
opciones: Both are supported — enable them in admin settings
It can block PRs but not fix them
It can fix but never block
Neither — it never approves or blocks, and there's no managed autofix; findings are applied locally with /code-review --fix
preguntas.explicacion: D. Las fronteras del servicio: nunca aprueba/bloquea (el juicio es humano) y no hay autofix administrado — el fix es local: /code-review --fix. "Claude flags things; you decide."

escenario.texto: Atlas Team is rolling Claude into its GitHub workflow — managed code review, a custom action, and shared plugins — while keeping unsupervised results trustworthy.

preguntas.stem: Atlas runs the claude-code-action on AWS Bedrock (use_bedrock: true). Does the workflow need the anthropic_api_key input?

Run both phases inside one long sleep-based script
Phase 1 outputs JSON; capture its session_id, and phase 2 runs claude --resume with it — full context restored
Impossible across separate invocations
preguntas.explicacion: C. 🔥 Reincidente #4: session_id + claude --resume — "one script kicks off the work, another resumes it later with full context". Un resumen pegado (A) pierde el razonamiento completo.

escenario.texto: Kappa Logistics is productionizing Claude Code: scripted runs, scheduled routines, and a review pipeline on GitHub.

preguntas.stem: A cron job must run Claude with the fastest startup and zero pickup of local hooks/skills/MCP/CLAUDE.md. Per the verified docs:
opciones: claude -p alone — print mode is already isolated
claude --bare -p "..." — --bare skips auto-discovery; plain -p loads the local environment
claude --headless --fast
Delete .claude/ before each run
preguntas.explicacion: B. Verificado contra docs: --bare salta la auto-discovery (y será el default de -p en el futuro — hoy no). La clavaste en el sim 3 — consolidando. ✔

escenario.texto: Kappa Logistics is productionizing Claude Code: scripted runs, scheduled routines, and a review pipeline on GitHub.

preguntas.stem: Which routine plan violates NONE of the three routine limits?
opciones: A security scan every 10 minutes, pushing patches to main
A dependency audit every 30 minutes on a claude/ branch
A daily report that pushes directly to main by default
A daily 9am Sentry triage that opens work on a claude/ prefixed branch
preguntas.explicacion: D. Los límites: research preview · recurrencia máximo cada hora (tumba A y B) · clone fresco que solo pushea a ramas claude/ por default (tumba A y C). Diaria + rama claude/ = ✔.

escenario.texto: Kappa Logistics is productionizing Claude Code: scripted runs, scheduled routines, and a review pipeline on GitHub.

preguntas.stem: Kappa's unattended nightly workflow uses claude-code-action. Which claude_args trio matches the course's tuning advice?
opciones: A --max-turns cap so the loop can't run forever · a permission mode that never stops to ask · allowed tools trimmed to exactly what the job needs (read-only for a report)
Maximum turns unlimited · bypass permissions · all tools enabled
--verbose logging · manual mode · full tool access
Streaming output · plan mode · no tools
preguntas.explicacion: A. Los 3 knobs: tope de turnos + modo que no pregunte (sin humano, un prompt cuelga el pipeline) + herramientas mínimas. Amarra L4 (modos) + curso 1 (allowed-tools).

escenario.texto: Kappa Logistics is productionizing Claude Code: scripted runs, scheduled routines, and a review pipeline on GitHub.

preguntas.stem: The security lead asks whether managed Code Review can be their enforcement gate: auto-blocking bad PRs and pushing fixes. Correct answer:
opciones: Yes — enable "strict mode" in the GitHub app
It blocks but the fix is manual
No — it only posts ranked, deduplicated findings; it never approves or blocks, and fixes are applied locally with /code-review --fix. For enforcement, wire your own checks
Yes, but only on enterprise plans
preguntas.explicacion: C. Las fronteras: señala, no decide — nunca aprueba/bloquea, sin autofix administrado. La clavaste 2 veces seguidas — cerrada. ✔

escenario.texto: Kappa Logistics is productionizing Claude Code: scripted runs, scheduled routines, and a review pipeline on GitHub.

preguntas.stem: An unattended overnight run produced a flawless-sounding summary. Rank the course's verification moves in the right spirit:
opciones: Trust the summary if the tests were reported green
Diff first (/code-review, then git diff, watching for files outside the plan) · tests wired as a gate, not a claim · cold second opinion from a fresh subagent for anything that matters
Ask the same session to double-check itself
Re-run the job and accept if both summaries agree
preguntas.explicacion: B. "The less you watched, the more you verify": diff antes que resumen · gates cableados (Stop+exit 2) · fresh eyes — la misma sesión (C) es juez y parte: "finds what the author rationalized away".

preguntas.stem: Your team requires that every file Claude Code writes is automatically checked by a formatter — with no exceptions, even if nobody asks for it. Which mechanism fits best?
opciones: A skill with a description mentioning "format files"
A PostToolUse hook matching Write/Edit tool calls
A CLAUDE.md rule stating "always format files"
A subagent dedicated to formatting
preguntas.explicacion: B. "Automatically… no exceptions… even if nobody asks" = evento + garantía = hook (PostToolUse sobre Write/Edit). Una skill (A) y CLAUDE.md (C) dependen del criterio de Claude — probabilístico; el subagent (D) no automatiza nada.

preguntas.stem: You clone a team repository that ships a code-review skill in .claude/skills/. You already have a personal code-review skill in ~/.claude/skills/. When you ask for a review, whose instructions apply?
opciones: The project skill — project settings are more specific than personal ones
The personal skill — personal has higher priority than project
Both are merged into one combined instruction set
Neither — Claude reports a conflict and asks you to choose
preguntas.explicacion: B. Prioridad E-P-P-P: Enterprise → Personal → Project → Plugins. La trampa es A ("más específico"): la intuición falla, Personal gana a Project. No hay merge (C) ni diálogo de conflicto (D).

preguntas.stem: At startup, what does Claude Code load into context from each available skill?
opciones: The full SKILL.md file of every skill
Only the name and description fields
The frontmatter plus the first 500 lines
Nothing — skills are only discovered when a request matches
preguntas.explicacion: B. Solo name + description — la base de la eficiencia de contexto. D describe mal el mecanismo: la lista SÍ se precarga, porque sin ella no habría contra qué hacer el matching.

preguntas.stem: A SKILL.md frontmatter contains only name and description. What can Claude do with tools while this skill is active?
opciones: Nothing — without allowed-tools, the skill cannot use any tools
Only read-only tools like Read and Grep
Anything its normal permission model allows — omitting allowed-tools means no restriction
Only the tools mentioned inside the skill's instructions
preguntas.explicacion: C. Omitir allowed-tools = sin restricción (modelo de permisos normal). A es la trampa clásica: "omitido" NO significa "sin herramientas".

preguntas.stem: Your skill's SKILL.md has grown to 1,900 lines, mostly large reference tables that only matter for rare edge cases. Following the open standard, what should you do?
opciones: Split it into two skills with different names
Move the tables to references/ files and link them from SKILL.md with an explicit "only load when..." condition
Raise the skill's model field so a larger model can handle the content
Compress the tables into shorter prose to fit under 500 lines
preguntas.explicacion: B. Progressive disclosure: SKILL.md < 500 líneas como índice + references/ con condición explícita "Only load when…". D pierde contenido; A fragmenta sin necesidad. No se recorta material: se decide CUÁNDO entra.

preguntas.stem: A skill includes a 300-line validation script in scripts/. What instruction should SKILL.md contain so the script stays context-efficient, and why?
opciones: "Read the script before running it" — so Claude understands what it does
"Run the script, not read it" — execution only puts the script's output into context
"Summarize the script" — a summary is cheaper than the full file
"Inline the script's logic into SKILL.md" — instructions are cheaper than code
preguntas.explicacion: B. "Tell Claude to run the script, not read it" — al ejecutar, solo el output consume tokens (300 líneas de código → quizá 3 de salida). Además el código probado es determinista.

preguntas.stem: A financial company must guarantee that a security-review skill is applied consistently by every developer, and that no developer can override it with their own version. Which distribution method?
opciones: Commit the skill to each team repository
Publish it as a plugin on an internal marketplace
Deploy it via enterprise managed settings
Email the skill folder to all developers to install personally
preguntas.explicacion: C. Keyword "must" + "no developer can override" = enterprise managed settings: prioridad máxima, pisa cualquier skill del mismo nombre. Repo (A) y plugin (B) quedan por debajo de Personal en prioridad.

preguntas.stem: You create a custom subagent in .claude/agents/reviewer.md and expect it to use your accessibility-audit skill, but it never applies it. What is the most likely cause?
opciones: The subagent's model field is set too low
Skills must be listed explicitly in the agent's skills: frontmatter field — subagents don't inherit skills
The skill needs allowed-tools to work inside subagents
Subagents can only use enterprise skills
preguntas.explicacion: B. El gotcha: los subagents no heredan skills — nacen con contexto limpio; hay que listarlas en skills:. Y recuerda: los built-in (Explore, Plan, Verify) no pueden usarlas en absoluto.

preguntas.stem: A skill exists, passes the validator, and appears in the available skills list — but Claude never uses it when you ask in your usual way. Per the course, what is the cause "almost always," and the fix?
opciones: A priority conflict — rename the skill
The description lacks overlap with how you phrase requests — add real trigger phrases
A YAML syntax error — re-run the validator
The skill is too long — apply progressive disclosure
preguntas.explicacion: B. "The cause is almost always the description" — falta overlap semántico; agrega las frases que TÚ realmente usas y prueba variaciones ("why is this slow?", "make this faster").

preguntas.stem: A skill loads fine but its script fails at runtime on Windows. Which pair of fixes does the course recommend?
opciones: Rename SKILL.md to skill.md and restart
Move the script to assets/ and reference it from the description
Give scripts execute permission (chmod +x) and use forward slashes ( / ) in all paths
Reinstall Claude Code and clear the plugin cache
preguntas.explicacion: C. Runtime errors: chmod +x a los scripts + forward slashes ( / ) incluso en Windows (+ dependencias instaladas y anotadas en la description).

tarjetas.cuerpo: Un PreToolUse tiene 4 salidas: allow / deny / ask… y la elegante: updatedInput — REESCRIBE la llamada (quita el secreto, el trabajo corre). Catch: reemplaza el input completo — devuelve también los campos que no cambias.

exit 2 = BLOQUEA (stderr se le entrega a Claude; puede bloquear incluso Stop).
exit 1 = NO bloquea 🪤 — se siente error pero Claude ejecuta igual. Para detener: 2, no 1.
Para que Claude NO pueda decir "terminé" con tests rotos: Stop hook que corre los tests y sale con exit 2 si fallan — el turno no termina y el stderr regresa a Claude, que arregla solo.
Para devolver contexto después de una compactación: SessionStart con matcher compact — su output SÍ vuelve a la conversación. PostCompact NO sirve para esto.
SOLO dentro de un contenedor o VM aislado. "Confío en mis prompts" NO es un control de seguridad. En tu laptop: auto mode (conserva al clasificador). Bypass = cero checks, ni clasificador.

Guarda INTENCIÓN, no CORRECCIÓN. Bloquea: deploys a prod, force push, pipe de código descargado, exfiltración. Deja pasar código ROTO — "broken isn't dangerous". El par completo: Auto (antes) + Stop hook con tests (después).

Manual (solo lee) · Accept edits (lee+edita+bash común; revisas después) · Plan (solo propone) · Auto (todo, con clasificador) · Don't ask (solo pre-aprobado; el resto se auto-deniega SIN prompt) · Bypass (sin checks — solo VM/contenedor).
En un pipeline sin humanos, un prompt de aprobación = pipeline colgado para siempre. Auto-denegar sin preguntar es la feature, no un defecto. CI / jobs nocturnos → Don't ask.

tarjetas.titulo: Hooks: la frase que lo define
tarjetas.cuerpo:
"Hooks turn a rule Claude usually follows into one it always follows."
CLAUDE.md y skills son instrucciones que Claude SIGUE; un hook es código que CORRE.

Con exit 0: el JSON en stdout se parsea; el texto plano se IGNORA… salvo en SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit y UserPromptExpansion, donde SE AGREGA al contexto (así funciona el hook preservador de estado).
Quien salta la auto-discovery (hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, CLAUDE.md) es --bare. -p a secas SÍ carga el entorno local. Receta para scripts limpios: claude --bare -p "...".
--output-format json --json-schema '...' → Claude RESTRINGE su salida al schema y el objeto cae en el campo structured_output → jq → base de datos.
Script A captura el session_id de su output JSON → script B corre claude --resume "$id" y retoma con todo el contexto. Un script planea, otro ejecuta.
1) Research preview (cambiará). 2) Recurrencia máximo cada hora. 3) Clone fresco del default branch que solo pushea a ramas claude/ — el guardrail anti-"reescribir main".
Routines (no construyes nada, infra de Anthropic) → -p (tu pipeline) → --bare (CI determinista) → Agent SDK (tu producto). "Start with routines; drop down only when the job needs the control."
Los 3 knobs: --max-turns (tope al loop) + permission mode que no pregunte (sin humano, un prompt cuelga todo) + allowed tools mínimas (un reporte = read-only).
NUNCA aprueba ni bloquea el PR (el juicio es humano) · SIN autofix administrado — aplicar findings es local: /code-review --fix · analiza el diff contra el codebase completo y deduplica/rankea.
anthropic_api_key es condicional: requerida SOLO con la Claude API directa. Con Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry / OAuth / WIF no se usa (autentican vía OIDC).
64 chars máx el name (minúsculas/números/guiones, = carpeta) · 1,024 chars máx la description · 500 líneas la guía para SKILL.md · 2 requeridos + 2 opcionales (allowed-tools, model).

Conflicto de NOMBRE entre skills: gana la de mayor prioridad —
Enterprise → Personal → Project → Plugins.
🪤 Personal le gana a Project (la intuición dice lo contrario). Plugins SIEMPRE al final.

tarjetas.titulo: La prioridad la define DÓNDE VIVE
tarjetas.cuerpo: Una skill de terceros copiada a ~/.claude/skills/ se vuelve Personal; copiada al repo, Project. "Plugins" solo aplica si llegó empaquetada en un plugin. Trade-off: plugin recibe updates; copia es tuya y editable.

Repo (.claude/skills commiteado → equipo, updates con git pull) → Plugin (marketplace → comunidad, no project-specific) → Enterprise (managed settings → keyword "MUST", compliance, pisa todo nombre igual).

tarjetas.titulo: Ciclo de activación de una skill
tarjetas.cuerpo: Arranque: carga solo name + description de 4 ubicaciones → tu petición se compara semánticamente (intención, no keywords) → match → confirmación → carga el SKILL.md completo. Cambios = reiniciar Claude Code.
Responde 2 preguntas: ¿qué hace? + ¿cuándo usarla? — con varias formulaciones reales ("Use when…"). Si no se dispara: agrega las frases que TÚ usas. Si dispara la equivocada: hazlas más distintas.
Los subagents NO heredan skills — nacen con "fresh, clean context". Hay que listarlas en el campo skills: del frontmatter. Si una opción dice "inherits"/"hereda" sobre subagents: desconfía.

Built-in (Explore, Plan, Verify): JAMÁS pueden usar skills.
Custom (.claude/agents/*.md): sí, pero solo las listadas en skills: (y con el tool Skill disponible).

tarjetas.titulo: Skills en subagent: carga al arrancar
tarjetas.cuerpo: En un subagent las skills listadas cargan AL ARRANCAR, todas completas — sin matching on-demand ni confirmación. Regla: "only list skills that are always relevant to the subagent's purpose".

OTRO Claude que nace en blanco, hace UNA tarea delegada en su contexto aislado y devuelve el resultado. Ganas aislamiento (50 archivos leídos nunca tocan TU contexto); pierdes historial y corrección a medio camino.
Skill que existe y pasa validación pero no se activa: "the cause is almost always the description" — falta overlap con tus frases. Prueba variaciones ("why is this slow?") y agrega las que fallen.

SKILL.md debe estar dentro de un directorio con nombre (no suelto en la raíz de skills/) y llamarse exactamente SKILL.md (SKILL mayúsculas, md minúsculas). Diagnóstico: claude --debug. Primero siempre: el validator (uv).
¿Tu skill personal es ignorada? Una de mayor prioridad tiene el mismo nombre (E-P-P-P). Camino fácil: renombrar la tuya a algo distinto ("frontend-review", no "review"). Plan B: hablar con el admin.

1) Dependencias instaladas (y anotadas en la description). 2) chmod +x a los scripts. 3) Forward slashes ( / ) en TODAS las rutas — incluso en Windows. Plugin sin skills: clear cache → restart → reinstall → validator.

"CLAUDE.md is not enforced configuration. It's guidance." Cada línea compite por atención — archivo gigante = reglas ignoradas. "The leaner the file, the more of it Claude follows." Hard rules → hooks.

Managed policy (inexcluible) + User + Project + Local (git-ignored): todos cargan JUNTOS al arrancar — "they stack, nothing gets dropped". 🪤 El contraste: la prioridad E-P-P-P es de SKILLS, no de CLAUDE.md.
Los imports @ruta/archivo de CLAUDE.md se expanden inline AL ARRANCAR — organizan, NO reducen el contexto. La carga diferida real es la de las skills (references/ con "Only load when…").

"IMPORTANT" y "YOU MUST" suben prioridad solo RELATIVO a lo que está en volumen normal. Si todo grita, nada resalta. Gasta el énfasis en las 2-3 reglas que más duelen al romperse. Y: regla específica y verificable + nombra el reemplazo.

"The less you watched, the more you verify." 1) Empieza por el DIFF, no el resumen ("a clean write-up is not proof of clean code"). 2) Tests como gate cableado, no promesa. 3) Cold second opinion: subagent fresco sin memoria del enfoque.

Un plugin corre código con TUS privilegios: instalas por sus skills y te llevas sus hooks — que se APILAN con los tuyos. Su clave agent puede promover un subagent al hilo PRINCIPAL. "Read before you install" · "reviewed isn't the same as trusted".

1 · Metadata (name+description — siempre cargado) → 2 · Instrucciones (cuerpo del SKILL.md — al activarse) → 3 · Recursos (references/ se LEEN · scripts/ se EJECUTAN · assets/ se USAN — solo si la tarea lo pide). "A table of contents in the context window."

/compact selecciona por TEMA y comprime TODO (dirígelo: di qué CONSERVAR; nunca toca disco).
Rewind-summarize selecciona por POSICIÓN (parte en un checkpoint; un lado queda literal; Rewind SÍ puede restaurar archivos). Doble Esc abre el menú.

tarjetas.titulo: /goal: el evaluador solo lee el transcript
tarjetas.cuerpo: La condición de /goal debe ser verificable en el output impreso: "pytest reports 0 failures" ✔ · "the code feels cleaner" ✘. Goal = CUÁNDO PARAR · Loop = CADA CUÁNTO MIRAR estado externo (CI, deploys).

Manos (sistema externo) → MCP · Espacio (ensuciaría tu contexto) → Subagent · Saber → ¿siempre? CLAUDE.md / ¿a veces? Skill · Nada, solo debe pasar → Hook.
Chequeo de seguridad: ¿toleras que a veces NO pase? No → Hook, sin importar lo demás.
